questions.question: The supervisor's salary in a factory is classified as:
options: Indirect labour — a factory overhead serving the factory as a whole
Direct labour — part of prime cost

questions.question: Under the perpetual inventory system:
options: Stock is only counted at year-end
Cost of sales is recorded at every sale, keeping the stock account continuously current
Cost of sales is deduced from a periodic count

questions.question: Depreciation on delivery vehicles is sorted into:
options: Selling and distribution cost — delivery serves sales, not production

questions.question: A wrong placement in the sorting table usually costs extra marks because:
options: It must be rewritten in ink
The statement totals downstream inherit the misfiled cost

questions.question: Opening raw materials R84 000, purchases R612 000, carriage R18 000, closing R90 000. Direct materials issued:
options: R624 000 — opening plus purchases plus carriage minus closing

questions.question: Factory wages are R390 000 and employer's contributions R30 000. Direct labour cost is:
options: R420 000 — the contributions ride on the factory wages

questions.question: Rent of R60 000 is split sixty percent factory by floor area. The production cost statement receives:
options: R36 000 — the remainder goes to administration
Nothing — rent is never a factory cost

questions.question: Total cost of production R1 376 000, opening work-in-progress R64 000, closing R48 000, 24 000 units finished. Unit cost:
options: R58,00 — cost of production of finished goods R1 392 000 over 24 000

questions.question: Selling price R80, variable costs R56. The contribution per mug is:
options: R24 — and it must use variable costs only

questions.question: Fixed costs R432 000 over contribution R24 gives a break-even of:
Last year: 17 500 mugs produced against a break-even of 17 800. The correct comment is:
options: The factory was profitable by 300 mugs
The factory fell 300 mugs short of break-even and made a loss; this year's 3 000-mug margin is the improvement
Break-even cannot be compared across years

questions.question: Producing 3 000 mugs beyond break-even at a R24 contribution yields a profit of:
options: R72 000 — fixed costs are already covered, so each extra mug drops its full contribution

questions.question: Two thousand five hundred units were available; six hundred remain; the last batch was nine hundred units at R80. FIFO closing stock is:
options: R48 000 — the units remaining are the newest, all from the R80 batch

questions.question: Total cost R180 000 over two thousand five hundred units gives a weighted average of:
options: R72,00 — closing stock of six hundred units at R43 200

questions.question: In a year of rising prices, FIFO compared to weighted average reports:
options: Lower closing stock and higher cost of sales
Higher closing stock, lower cost of sales, and therefore higher profit

questions.question: Six hundred units on hand against sales of 1 900 a year is about 115 days of stock. The judgement depends on:
options: The sales rhythm — seasonal peaks may justify it; flat demand makes it sleeping capital and a theft risk

questions.question: March sales R210 000, thirty percent cash. Cash sales receipts for March are:
February credit sales were R133 000, collected sixty percent the month after sale. March receives:
options: R79 800 — plus R36 750 from January's credit sales at thirty-five percent

questions.question: The five percent of credit sales that turns bad appears in the cash budget:
options: As a receipt in the third month
Nowhere — bad debts move no cash; they belong to the projected income statement
As a note to the budget

questions.question: Budgeted advertising R12 000, actual R5 000, and sales fell short. The managerial comment is:
options: The underspend likely caused the shortfall — advertising is seed, not luxury; restore and monitor it

subtopics.title: The Reconciliation and Age Analysis Task

questions.question: Our payment of R9 800 made on the last day of the month is missing from the supplier's statement. The correction is:
options: Subtract R9 800 on the statement side — a timing difference

questions.question: The statement overcharges R450 against the agreed price. This is corrected by:
options: Subtracting R450 on the statement side — their error, their side

questions.question: An unrecorded debit note for returns of R2 000 is corrected by:
options: Subtracting R2 000 from our ledger — our omission, our side, reaching the agreed R62 550

questions.question: On thirty-day terms, R36 000 sits at sixty days and R18 000 at ninety-plus in an R180 000 book. A full-mark response includes:
options: Praising the forty-five percent that is current
Interest on arrears, suspending the oldest accounts, credit checks, early-settlement discounts — and separating cash receiving from ledger keeping

subtopics.title: The VAT, Internal Control and Ethics Task

questions.question: Sales of R560 000 excluding VAT produce output tax of:
The owner takes stock costing R4 000 excluding VAT. The settlement adjustment is:
options: Add R600 — the input claim on consumed goods must be returned

questions.question: A debtor owing R6 900 including VAT is written off. The vendor reclaims:
options: R1 035 — fifteen percent of the debt
Nothing — bad debts are not a VAT matter
R900 — fifteen over one hundred and fifteen, because the figure is inclusive

questions.question: A private notebook that lets weekend cash sales bypass the record is best described as:
options: A private matter for the owner
VAT fraud and tax evasion — money held in trust for SARS is being stolen, and the understated records mislead every user
